checks: For R>2 the projection contains exactly the integers zero and one. The left and right roof lines meet their respective sampled planes at height one, and the floor is at minus one.
The exposed-base pointwise theorem makes the raw maximum one on either interval. At (0,0), the fixed cap x≥z has length one on base zero and only a null endpoint on base one, giving fraction 1/4.

Solving the two roof intersections with x=z gives the left point (−1/(2R−3),−1/(2R−3)) and the right point (1,1). Determinants give the two area formulas in the draft and the limit from their leading coefficients. Rational polygon replay agreed at several values of R.
Original §5, (12) uses the same interpolation, sampled cap, areas and limit.

dependencies.mapping: Each of zero and one is exposed in the complete positive-volume base set. In the two length-two interval fibers, the midpoint maximizes intrinsic depth with value one.

overlap.comparison: Gives exact exposed-fiber intrinsic depth, which fixes the mixed maximum here. It does not constrain ambient interpolation or give the ambient cap limit.

readability: The fixed cap is optimal at the original mixed mark for every R, and the ambient area ratio varies through the interpolation.

summary: The two sampled intervals and the minimizing mixed cap stay fixed as the ambient cap fraction tends to one.
